base.name: (s3c-ann-net)
base.is: repo_model.s3c_announced.ANN_NET_ARM walked by repo_model.spread_mr_state_calendar.walk on direct pairs, its quantiles capped at the SRF line as (s3c) (repo_model.s3c_candidate), exactly as scripts/s3c_flagnet_gross_1321.py walks and caps its reference (ANNNET): the frame, decision days, tables, states and caps are #1255's, #1273's, #1288's and #1321's as merged
base.walk: minimum history and refit cadence of that family (refit every 21 decision days); the plus arms are walked on the same decision days, tables and refit blocks

targets.source: metadata/richer_targets_706.json, choice.chosen; the targets, model class (candidate (b) of #634), minimum history 61, refit every 21 days, leads 1 to 5, 23-level law and direct pairs (amendment of #932) are #706's
targets.forecasts: the fifteen walks of scripts/richer_targets_706.py, redone at 18:00 on the 18:00 scratch panel by `target-walk` (the same walk, pinned), each refused by `check_target_walk` unless it names this target and lead, instant 18:00, the declared scratch panel, this declaration and direct pairs

input.form: one value per target and lead: the median (level 0.5 of the 23-level grid, target_forecasts.median_of) of the target's lead-h law for the target day h business days after the decision day, in the target's unit divided by a declared scale (UNITS: bgcr_dispersion_bps 1 (bp), sofr_dispersion_bps 1 (bp), on_rrp_change_bn 100 (USD billions to USD 100 bn, the unit of the settlement sizes)), as one extra term of the arm (spread_mr_state_calendar.H9_FORECAST), beside the two net settlement terms. No other function of the law (width, tail level, mean), no interaction with the state, and no combination of targets is declared or tried
input.alignment: direct pairs: the training pair of target row t reads s3c_h9.TargetForecastTable.at(lead, t), the forecast made on decision row t - lead for t; a forecast reads read(lead, decision_index), the same decision's own forecast for its target row. The value is the one the walk made, never another day's (a decision day without a forecast serves nothing)
input.availability: public at the 18:00 decision instant of the decision day (metadata/sources_measurement.json, h9_target_forecasts, zero lag). Each forecast comes from a fit made at or before that instant: TargetForecastTable refuses, with LookAheadError, a forecast whose recorded fit (rebuilt by target_forecasts.fit_decision_dates from the fold grid and refit blocks the walk used) is after its own decision day or has none
input.holes: a decision day with no forecast of the target (the first 61 labels of the target walk, a lead with no law) serves nothing. The fit centres the term on its mean over the training pairs that have it and gives a pair without it the value of that mean, so a hole is neither a zero forecast nor another day's; the term enters a refit only if at least 61 training pairs have it (spread_mr_state_calendar.H9_MIN_OBSERVED), otherwise the plus arm's refit is the base's to the bit (tested). The share of scored cells whose refit had the term is reported per lead
input.fit: the arm's own Huber fit (threshold 1.345 robust standard deviations, ridge 5 pseudo-days on every term coefficient, none on the intercept), the target in scale units (raw residual over the scale at the pair's origin), so the coefficient is in scale units per unit of the scaled forecast; the effect in bp is the coefficient times the anchor's scale. Nothing about the base's terms changes

variants.(s3c-ann-net): the base, unchanged from #1288/#1321: no new fit
variants.(s3c-ann-net)+bgcr_dispersion_bps: the base and the lead-h median of the BGCR dispersion walk as one centred extra term, on direct pairs
variants.(s3c-ann-net)+on_rrp_change_bn: the base and the lead-h median of the ON RRP daily change walk (USD 100 bn) as one centred extra term, on direct pairs
variants.(s3c-ann-net)+sofr_dispersion_bps: the base and the lead-h median of the SOFR dispersion walk as one centred extra term, on direct pairs
variants.count: three added fits (the plus arms), one per target. The fifteen target walks are #706's redone at 18:00 and add no variant of the base. No hyperparameter differs from the arm's, no form of the input is tried besides the one declared

protocol.primary_score: grid CRPS over the protocol's 23 levels, equal weight over h = 1 to 5, one number per decision day
protocol.nested_difference: d = S(base) - S(base + target); positive favours the target's forecast; skill = mean(d) / mean(S(base))
protocol.interval: studentized stationary bootstrap (Newey-West lag 10), mean block 10, the protocol's draws, seed 1345, one-sided 95% lower bound on mean d (scripts/spread_mr_variants_761.run_pairs, the test #1288 and #1321 use); a group whose forecasts are identical is reported as identical
protocol.multiplicity: Holm across the three targets on the pooled primary score, on the Diebold-Mariano one-sided p-value the paired row carries (the bootstrap p of #932 is not in that row); nothing here is a claim
protocol.splits: pooled; without decision day 2019-09-18 (#798; every split group holding it is also read without it); by lead; by regime of the target day (metadata/evaluation_splits.json); by pressure-day type of the target day. No split is a pass requirement; a group of fewer than 20 decision days is not tested

reading_rule.per_target: as #842 and #932: a target's forecast IMPROVES the candidate when the one-sided 95% lower bound of mean(d) on the pooled primary score is above zero; otherwise 'no improvement beyond its interval', with the point skill beside it. Both with and without 2019-09-18; both stated if they differ. A split cell that shows a gain is reported with the number of cells read, never alone
reading_rule.h9_kill_clause: the page states each target's reading; it does not read H9's kill clause ("no nested gain for H5"). That reading is Eleonora's

marked_questions.question: How does a target's forecast enter (s3c-ann-net)? (s3c-ann-net) is a Huber regression of volatility-scaled residuals on settlement terms, not a gradient-boosted model, so 'add the target's forecast as an input' needs a form. Declared: one extra term, the lead-h median in the target's unit over a fixed scale, centred on its training mean, fitted with the arm's own Huber and ridge-5 penalty.
options: (1) as declared: the median, centred, one coefficient per lead
(2) the median relative to the target's as-of value (a forecast change, not a level), which needs a new as-of read of each target
(3) a stacked check instead: regress the base's pinball residual on the forecast, outside the fit
marked_questions.default: (1). It changes no claim; a different form is a new declaration and a re-run of the plus arms only (minutes, not the target walks)
